messages:
maria: Heads up — EU1 GPU pool is trending to ~95% util in the next 8–12h. p99 queueing risk for low-latency routes. Forecast shows ~2.2k extra GPU-hours next week because of the marketing campaign + batch retrains. We should either tighten admission or spin up extra capacity.
jon: Can you drop the current numbers (GPUs, baseline GPU-hrs/day, observed p95/p99)? Need to see the math before we change admit curves.
maria: Current raw: 320 A100s in EU1 (12h rolling avg). Baseline usage ~= 320*24 = 7680 GPU-hrs/day. Yesterday peak used ~88% sustained, now trending. Observed p95 ~120ms, p99 ~420ms for latency-sensitive endpoints. Arrival rate jumped ~28% since 06:00 UTC.
jon: If we assume service rate mu per GPU = 30 reqs/s (avg for the mix) and target util u <= 0.85 to keep tail reasonable, admitted lambda must be <= mu * GPUs * u. Quick calc: 30 * 320 * 0.85 ~= 8160 reqs/s admitted capacity. What's current lambda?
maria: Current modeled lambda (observed) ~= 9500 reqs/s at peak windows. So delta ~1340 reqs/s over safe admit. That maps roughly to the projected 2.2k GPU-hrs/week when integrated across batch durations and throughput.
devon: Options: 1) change admit curve to start shedding non-critical routes at 0.9->0.85 util hysteresis, 2) prewarm N GPUs (short term), 3) route some traffic to smaller quantized variants. My preference is a mix: soft admission + quick prewarm.
alina: Prewarm economics: if we prewarm 40 GPUs for 6 hours (buffer for the afternoon spike) cost estimate = 40 * $2.5/hr * 6 = $600. That buys ~40*6 = 240 GPU-hrs of runway and reduces coldstart churn. Also reduces queueing amplification.
jon: For admission config, propose soft drop for background/low-priority models first (70% of shed), then sample degrade enterprise routes only if we hit critical. Need a quick admit policy patch.
devon: Proposed admit snippet (will test in staging):
```yaml
admission_control:
  mode: soft_hysteresis
  upper_util: 0.90
  lower_util: 0.80
  shed_order:
    - background_batch
    - low_priority_inference
    - noninteractive_rerank
  sample_rate_on_shed: 0.05
```
jon: Looks good. Also reduce batch size for latency-sensitive routes from 16->8 to lower service time variance. That will raise tokens/sec slightly but improves p99.
maria: Can we also enable immediate fallback to the 8-bit quantized variant for 25% of requests when admit hits >0.92? That gives headroom without full reject. Tradeoff: slight quality drop.
alina: I ran a quick rollback cost calc for using dedicated burst instances instead of prewarm: spinning 50 spot GPUs for 4h @ $1.2/hr = $240, but risk of spot evict. If we need guaranteed SLAs, prewarm reserved is safer.
sre-bot: autoscaler: scale_request accepted — adding 50 GPUs to eu1-pool, ETA 18 minutes. (triggered by policy: sustained 15m util > 0.88)
maria: OK action items: (1) devon patch admit config to staging with the YAML above (test window + metrics), (2) jon run admission-rate simulation for p99 with current arrival spike (use M/M/c rough model + measured svc var), (3) alina confirm prewarm budget approval ($600 cap) and start prewarm schedule, (4) ops monitor autoscaler rollup and rollback if spot churn. I'll be on watch — callout if p99 > 500ms. :thumbsup:
